title: Diagnosing Data Quality Before AI Workflows Scale (2026)

questions.question: Which dimension has the largest weight in DomainProfile.weighted_score?
options: Uniqueness, weighted 0.45 because duplicate master records are especially harmful
Completeness, weighted 0.50 because null fields dominate every workflow
Timeliness, weighted 0.45 because stale records are always blocking
All three dimensions are weighted equally at one third
questions.explanation: WEIGHTS assigns 0.30 to completeness, 0.45 to uniqueness, and 0.25 to timeliness. The scorer deliberately gives duplicate-record risk the greatest influence.

questions.question: What verdict does assess assign to the Supplier / vendor domain at HIGH criticality?
options: DEPLOY, because its completeness score is above 0.80
CONDITIONAL, because its weighted score is about 0.700: above the 0.65 floor but below 0.90
BLOCK, because any duplicate rate above 30% bypasses the aggregate score
DEPLOY, because high criticality lowers the deploy threshold
questions.explanation: The supplier scores 0.82 completeness, 0.62 uniqueness, and 0.70 timeliness, for 0.700 overall. HIGH criticality makes 0.90 the deploy threshold and 0.65 the block floor, so the result is CONDITIONAL.

questions.question: Why is Customer / party CONDITIONAL at HIGH criticality even though its score is close to 0.90?
options: Its 4% null rate is below the completeness floor, so the domain is blocked
Timeliness is the weakest dimension and requires a daily refresh before any pilot
Its weighted score is about 0.892, below the 0.90 deploy threshold; uniqueness is weakest and calls for entity resolution
The high-criticality policy ignores weighted scores and always returns CONDITIONAL
questions.explanation: Customer / party scores 0.892 from 0.96 completeness, 0.82 uniqueness, and 0.94 timeliness. It misses the HIGH deploy threshold by a small margin, with uniqueness identified as the weakest dimension and the mitigation target.

questions.question: What verdict does the Product catalogue receive at HIGH criticality?
options: CONDITIONAL, because every high-criticality domain needs an inference-time filter
BLOCK, because its 8% stale rate exceeds the 6% compliance window
CONDITIONAL, because uniqueness is below 1.0
DEPLOY, because its weighted score is about 0.961 and clears the 0.90 threshold
questions.explanation: The product catalogue scores 0.98 completeness, 0.97 uniqueness, and 0.92 timeliness, yielding roughly 0.961. That exceeds the HIGH deploy threshold, so no conditional mitigation is added.

questions.question: A new high-criticality domain has null_rate=0.10, duplicate_rate=0.20, and stale_rate=0.05. What verdict follows?
options: CONDITIONAL, because its weighted score is about 0.868, below the 0.90 deploy threshold
DEPLOY, because every dimension is at least 0.80
BLOCK, because a 20% duplicate rate is below the hard block floor
DEPLOY, because timeliness carries the largest weight
questions.explanation: The component scores are 0.90, 0.80, and 0.95. The weighted total is 0.30*0.90 + 0.45*0.80 + 0.25*0.95 = 0.8675, which is conditional at HIGH criticality.

questions.question: What mitigation does assess recommend when uniqueness is the weakest dimension in a CONDITIONAL result?
options: Add a null-field filter and expose confidence when required fields are absent
Run entity resolution before indexing and restrict retrieval to golden-record IDs
Refresh the source daily and filter records newer than 90 days
Raise the deploy threshold until duplicate records disappear from the report
questions.explanation: _mitigation_advice maps uniqueness to entity-resolution preprocessing and golden-record filtering. That addresses duplicate master records before they create contradictory retrieval evidence.
